brief_text: Margaret T. is a 74-year-old member discharged on 08/18/2026 after a 4-day admission for acute-on-chronic systolic heart failure. Her 30-day readmission risk is elevated (score 0.87 — High-Risk / Complex), driven by three ED visits in the past 90 days, a CHF + CKD + diabetes comorbidity cluster, a new IV-to-oral diuretic conversion, and limited caregiver support. Discharge labs showed markedly elevated NT-proBNP (2,450 pg/mL) and borderline potassium (3.4 mEq/L) on high-dose furosemide, and her cardiology follow-up was not scheduled before she left the hospital. Recommend outreach within 48 hours, confirmation of a cardiology appointment within 7 days, a BMP in 5–7 days, and enrollment in the high-intensity post-discharge pathway per playbook §4.1.
outreach_message: Hello Margaret, this is your Humana care coordination team checking in after your recent hospital stay. We want to make sure your recovery at home is going smoothly. Please remember to weigh yourself each morning, follow your fluid and sodium guidelines, and take your new water pill (furosemide) twice a day as prescribed. We would like to help you schedule your heart doctor visit within the next week and a quick blood draw to check your potassium. If you gain more than 2 pounds overnight, feel more short of breath, or notice new swelling, please call us right away at the number on your member card. Can we confirm a good time to talk this week? We are here to help.

brief_text: James R. is a 61-year-old member discharged on 08/20/2026 after a 3-day admission for an acute COPD exacerbation. His 30-day readmission risk is moderate (score 0.54 — Medium-Risk), driven by two COPD admissions in the past year, active tobacco use, a new home oxygen order, and a 14-day prednisone taper. SpO2 at discharge was borderline (89% on room air), but his pulmonology follow-up on 09/02/2026 is already confirmed, and he has strong caregiver support from his spouse. Recommend outreach within 72 hours to verify oxygen equipment delivery (scheduled 08/21), review the steroid taper schedule, and offer tobacco cessation program enrollment per playbook §5.2.
outreach_message: Hello James, this is your Humana care coordination team following up on your recent hospital stay for your breathing. We want to confirm your oxygen equipment was delivered on Friday and that you are comfortable using it. Please keep taking your prednisone exactly on the taper schedule your care team gave you, and keep using your daily inhaler even on good days. Your lung doctor visit is already set for September 2nd. If you feel more short of breath, notice your oxygen readings dropping below 88%, or have a fever, please call us right away. We would also be glad to tell you about our free program to help members quit smoking whenever you are ready. Is now a good time for a quick check-in?

If you develop a fever over 100.4°F, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or worsening belly pain, please call your surgeon or us right away. Is there anything we can help you with today?
